recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中央是一顆雙葉核的嗜酸性球，其胞質中的橘紅色顆粒偏少且分布不均、夾雜淡灰藍區域；紅血球大致正常。單一視野無法確立嗜酸性球增多，需結合血球計數與PDGFRA基因檢測。
features: Single eosinophil with a bilobed nucleus with two round, symmetric lobes
Orange-red granules relatively sparse and unevenly distributed with pale agranular areas (mild hypogranulation)
Background red cells normocytic and normochromic with mild anisocytosis; one polychromatic red cell
Scattered normal-appearing platelets; no blasts in this low-power field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an eosinophil with a bilobed nucleus and relatively sparse, unevenly distributed eosinophilic granules with pale agranular cytoplasmic areas. The red cells are predominantly normocytic and normochromic with mild anisocytosis and an occasional polychromatic cell, and platelets appear adequate in number and morphology. No blasts are seen in this field. A single field cannot establish marked eosinophilia; however, in conjunction with the reported marked eosinophilia with abnormal granulation and segmentation and FIP1L1::PDGFRA fusion, the findings are consistent with a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with PDGFRA rearrangement.

ddx.vs: Reactive eosinophils can show the same mild hypogranulation, so separation depends on clinical workup for secondary causes and absence of PDGFRA/PDGFRB/FGFR1 rearrangements.
Idiopathic HES has persistent eosinophilia with end-organ damage but no identifiable clonal genetic abnormality or aberrant T-cell population.
Basophils have coarse dark purple-black granules obscuring the nucleus rather than orange-red refractile granules.
